item.research_question: Can single-source precursors be used to synthesize metastable fcc-structured refractory binary alloys that lie within miscibility gaps, and how do their compressibility and structural stability compare to ideal solution models under high pressure?
item.processing_route: Thermal decomposition of single-source precursors in gaseous hydrogen flow at temperatures below 800 °C (specifically 400–700 °C depending on the precursor); precursors synthesized from aqueous solutions at room temperature.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression up to 50 GPa in diamond anvil cells using Helium as a pressure transmitting medium; X-ray diffraction at ID15B beamline (λ = 0.411235 Å).
key_findings: fcc–Ir0.50Pt0.50 and fcc–Rh0.50Pd0.50 are metastable alloys corresponding to miscibility gaps on binary metallic phase diagrams.
fcc–Ir0.50Pt0.50 has an atomic volume V0/Z = 14.597(6) Å3·atom−1, bulk modulus B0 = 321(6) GPa, and B0' = 6(1).
fcc–Rh0.66Pt0.33 has an atomic volume V0/Z = 14.211(3) Å3·atom−1, bulk modulus B0 = 259(1) GPa, and B0' = 6.66(9).
fcc–Rh0.50Pd0.50 has an atomic volume V0/Z = 14.18(2) Å3·atom−1, bulk modulus B0 = 223(4) GPa, and B0' = 5.0(3).
All investigated fcc-structured binary alloys are stable under compression up to 50 GPa with no pressure-induced phase transitions.
Atomic volumes and bulk moduli show good agreement with the ideal solutions model for most alloys.
Thermal decomposition of [Ir(NH3)5Cl][PtBr6] in inert atmosphere forms IrBr3 as an intermediate, leading to two-phase mixtures, unlike hydrogen flow which yields single-phase alloys.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that thermal decomposition in hydrogen flow allows for the formation of single-phase alloys even within miscibility gaps, whereas inert atmospheres lead to two-phase mixtures due to the formation of metal bromide intermediates (e.g., IrBr3) that decompose differently. The compressibility behavior is explained by the alloys acting as ideal solid solutions, where atomic volumes and bulk moduli follow linear or predictable concentration dependencies.
item.limitations: The text notes that fcc–Ir0.50Pt0.50 and fcc–Pt0.33Rh0.67 show large deviations from the ideal solutions model, and the deviation for fcc–Ir0.50Pt0.50 may be explained by relatively low experimental pressure, while the deviation for fcc–Pt0.33Rh0.67 requires further theoretical study.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that the mentioned large deviation from the ideal solutions model should be further studied theoretically and that diverse single-source precursors should be designed to prepare useful functional alloys as nanostructured powders for catalytic applications.
quotes: Fcc–Ir0.50Pt0.50 and fcc–Rh0.50Pd0.50 correspond to miscibility gaps on binary metallic phase diagrams and can be considered as metastable alloys.
Such Br…Br contacts were responsible for the packing of anions in the crystal structure as it was shown for other structures with hexabromometallates (IV).
